title: Five-pillar building
subject: Islamic Studies
unit: Spring 1: Islam and the five pillars
source: Written for islamic-studies/y1 lesson 7 (Pupil PDF worksheet: five-pillar building)
intro: Lesson 7: The five pillars of Islam. Listen, look, then do the tasks with a grown-up.

panels.title: Islam is built on five
points: The Prophet ﷺ said Islam is built on five
Like five pillars holding up a building

blocks.h: The five pillars on five fingers

box.title: Draw a building held up by five pillars. Write one pillar on each: shahadah, salah, zakah, sawm, hajj.

keywords.def: a strong post that holds a building up
our way of life: obeying Allah
saying Allah is One and Muhammad ﷺ is His Messenger
the prayer five times a day

questions.q: Say the five pillars on your fingers.
Draw a building with five pillars. Write one pillar on each.
questions.a: Five pillars labelled: shahadah, salah, zakah, sawm, Hajj

questions.q: Extend: tick the pillar you can do every day.
Stretch: why does the house need all five pillars?
questions.a: Without one, it is not complete and strong.

questions.q: Which pillar is praying five times a day?
questions.a: A) Salah. Salah is prayer. Hajj is the journey to Makkah; zakah is giving.

questions.q: How many pillars of Islam are there?
Think again: what happens if a pillar is missing?
questions.a: The building is not strong. We need all five pillars.
